title: A statistical approach to bias in zero-shot learning: the lens of handwriting recognition
abstract: arXiv:2609.10084v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generalized zero-shot learning (GZSL) has emerged as an important paradigm for visual recognition systems that must generalize to classes that were not observed during training. Traditional GZSL techniques are limited by their applicability to a relatively small number of such unseen classes, scalability beyond which is challenging due to its well-known misclassification bias towards classes observed during training. In this work, we investigate the GZSL paradigm through the lens of zero-shot handwritten word recognition over extremely large vocabularies. We propose a statistical approach to rectifying this bias, which views any classical GZSL feature learner as a black box mechanism whose intrinsic bias in identifying the training status (seen vs. unseen) of a typical data point we aim to correct, similar to an out of distribution inferential problem. tldr: 本文提出一种统计方法，将传统GZSL特征学习器视为黑盒并纠正其在判别数据点训练状态（已见/未见）时的固有偏差，从而实现了超大词汇表上的零样本手写单词识别。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a statistical approach that treats any classical GZSL feature learner as a black box and corrects its intrinsic bias in identifying the training status (seen vs. unseen) of data points, enabling zero-shot handwritten word recognition over extremely large vocabularies.
